problem_statement: technext/restaurant-html-template, rebranded here as Copperleaf Kitchen (a seasonal neighbourhood restaurant with breakfast, plated mains and garden salads), is a static Bootstrap site served from index.html plus local css/, js/, images/ and fonts/ (no build step). The site now spans a home page (index.html) and two shared-nav secondary pages, menu.html and reservations.html. Deliver a coordinated 'order the menu' experience while preserving the Bootstrap shell, the nav, the scripts and the responsive behaviour: (1) On the home page, build an 'Order the menu' section (#menu) with the restaurant's own menu GRID of six dishes (each a card with a name, price, description and course tag) and a course FILTER (All dishes / Breakfast / Mains / Salads). Clicking a course must FILTER the grid to that course AND update the '#menu-readout' count to 'Showing <n> of 6 · <Course>' (e.g. clicking Mains shows the two mains and reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · Mains'); the pre-click default is 'Showing 6 of 6 · All dishes'. REPAIR the grid so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow — do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width, and the cards must never shingle or overlap into an illegible pile. (2) Promote the course vocabulary into a shared 'Reservations desk' rail (Breakfast / Mains / Salads course tiles) that appears CONSISTENTLY on the home menu section AND on the menu.html AND reservations.html pages, styled to match the Copperleaf ivory/copper palette (light surface, copper accents, readable text) — the rendered rail must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette dark slab. (3) Keep the menu cards legible: dish names, prices and descriptions must have real contrast against the card surface (no near-white text on a near-white card). Keep the hero, about, journal/blog, subscribe, contact block, footer, scripts and desktop/tablet layout intact, and keep the site static with a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font/map requests).
required_content: An 'Order the menu' section (#menu) is added to the home page with a six-dish menu grid (cards with name / price / description / course tag) and a course filter row (All dishes / Breakfast / Mains / Salads) plus a '#menu-readout' count, all rendering within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px and no overlapping cards.

Clicking a course filter FILTERS the menu grid to that course AND updates '#menu-readout' to 'Showing <n> of 6 · <Course>' (clicking Mains shows two cards and reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · Mains'); the post-click terminal state reflects the selected course, not the default 'Showing 6 of 6 · All dishes'.

A shared 'Reservations desk' rail (Breakfast / Mains / Salads course tiles) appears CONSISTENTLY on the home menu section AND on the menu.html AND reservations.html pages — the same rail component in all three places, not only on the home page.

The 'Reservations desk' rail and the menu cards keep the Copperleaf ivory/copper palette (light surface, copper accents, readable text) and are visually faithful to the reference rendering — the grid is a clean wrapped layout, not a collapsed/overlapping pile, and the cards are legible (no near-white text on a near-white surface).

The menu.html and reservations.html secondary pages share the home navigation and remain reachable (real routes, not 404), and the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports.
The hero, about, journal/blog, subscribe, contact block and footer remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font/map errors).
design_constraints: Build the menu grid as a responsive layout that wraps on mobile; do not use a fixed-width non-wrapping row, and do not shingle the cards with negative margins.

Add the SAME shared 'Reservations desk' rail component to the home menu section, the menu.html page AND the reservations.html page so the course language is consistent site-wide; do not add it to only one page.
Preserve the Copperleaf/Bootstrap design language: existing section rhythm, nav, ivory/copper accent, rounded cards; the rail and cards must render in the ivory/copper palette with legible text.
Keep the course filter wired end to end (the #menu-readout terminal count must reflect the clicked course and the grid must actually filter), not merely a class toggle.

Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console, and the secondary pages must share the same nav and stay real routes.
state_constraints: desktop_initial verifies the RedStore home page, navigation, hero, and product discovery remain visible.
mobile_initial verifies the RedStore home page and menu shell at 390px before flow changes.
tablet_initial verifies the RedStore home page at an intermediate viewport.
desktop_products verifies the products page, sorting dropdown, product grid, and first product link remain visible.
desktop_product_detail verifies product gallery, size selector, quantity input, Add To Cart button, and product details remain visible.
desktop_add_to_cart_flow clicks Add To Cart from product_details.html and verifies the cart state handoff is reachable through the shopping flow.
desktop_cart verifies the cart table, totals, cart state handoff, account checkout link, and keep-shopping link.
mobile_cart verifies the cart state handoff and cart table stack without horizontal overflow at 390px.
desktop_account verifies the handoff target page still contains Login and Register surfaces.

change_completion: The menu grid renders its six dishes within the viewport on mobile with no overlap.
The shared 'Reservations desk' rail appears on the home menu section, the menu.html page AND the reservations.html page.
The course filter click filters the grid and updates the #menu-readout count to the selected course.
design_consistency: The Copperleaf ivory/copper palette, section rhythm, accent color and nav are preserved.
The 'Reservations desk' rail and menu cards keep the ivory/copper look, are legible, and are visually faithful to the reference across the home + secondary pages.
regression: Hero, about, journal/blog, subscribe, contact and footer remain reachable and unchanged.
The static site serves from index.html + menu.html + reservations.html with a clean console.
responsive: 390px home (initial, menu) and the mobile menu page have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px; 834px tablet is clean.
The menu cards wrap or stack cleanly instead of forcing a fixed-width overflowing row or an overlapping pile.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static multi-page commerce task on the reassigned technext restaurant template (rebranded Copperleaf Kitchen), hardened to L4 with a genre-native menu-ordering lever. The reference (a) builds an 'Order the menu' section whose six-dish menu grid WRAPS to a clean responsive layout on mobile (CSS grid -> 0 overflow) with legible ivory/copper cards, (b) promotes a shared 'Reservations desk' rail onto the home menu section AND the menu.html AND reservations.html pages in the ivory/copper palette, and (c) wires the course filter so clicking a course filters the grid AND #menu-readout reads 'Showing <n> of 6 · <Course>'. The baseline is the original layout defect: a fixed 900px non-wrapping grid row (overflows mobile ~1405px), NO rail anywhere (D2 fails on all three pages, D3 fails) but the filter JS is CORRECT (baseline PASSES D4 -> leg-orthogonal). The bad 'smart-wrong' solution shingles the cards with negative margins into an overlapping illegible pile and paints near-white text on near-white cards (D3 visual_regression fail: a whole-grid geometry break, not a recolor), narrows the grid to min-width:560px + overflow-x:hidden so it still overflows the document ~185px on mobile (D6 fail), adds the rail to the HOME page only (D2 cross-page fail on menu.html + reservations.html) as a dark collapsed slab, and toggles the filter .active class without filtering the grid or re-counting #menu-readout (click succeeds but the readout stays 'Showing 6 of 6 · All dishes' -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). bad fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. The secondary pages load a minimal own script set so the shared page runs pageerror-free on all legs (declared INFRA, identical across the three legs). WOW.js entrance animations are neutralized via CSS (INFRA) so page-top screenshots carry no phantom horizontal translate.
